We ensured that Design for Manufacturing and tolerance stack - up analysis guided fixture design, process planning, and inspection strategy. Quality and risk were managed through PFMEA, control plans, and SOPs, while cost, productivity, and traceability were ensured for all parts. The manufacturing workflow reflects OEM and Tier - 1 industry practices, designed to support consistent and scalable mass production of 4,000 units per annum. 1. DESIGN FOR MANUFACTURING : - Design for Manufacturing DFM\ emphasises ease of production, consistency, and minimum cost while meeting functional requirements. In a gearbox, DFM ensures the design aligns with practical manufacturing processes, tooling, and tolerances. The gearbox casing is typically manufactured by casting, where uniform wall thickness promotes even cooling, minimises internal stresses, and reduces defects such as shrinkage and porosity. Appropriate casting allowances shrinkage, machining, and draft are incorporated. Gears are produced by hobbing, and the use of standardised modules, pressure angles, and optimised face widths simplifies geometry, reducing machining time, tooling costs, and overall manufacturing complexity. 1.2. DFM/DFA justification Design for Manufacturing DFM\ The Gearbox components are designed for ease of manufacturing by maintaining uniform wall thickness, smooth transitions, and adequate fillet radii, improving castability and reducing defects such as shrinkage and porosity. Standardised shaft diameters, gear modules, hole sizes, and tolerances allow the use of manufacturing processes like turning, drilling, milling, and hobbing with standard tooling. Clear datums and dimensional layouts simplify inspection and ensure repeatability. The use of Al alloys enhances machinability, surface finish, and reduces machining time and overall cost. Design for Assembly DFA\ The Gearbox assembly is simplified through a modular layout that enables sequential assembly with minimal part reorientation and handling. Standardised bearings and fasteners reduce part variety and assembly errors. Self - locating features such as shoulders, spacers, and bearing seats ensure correct axial positioning of gears and shafts without adjustments. Adequate clearances for tools and clear alignment of mating components improve assembly speed, reduce labour effort, and enhance reliability and consistency of the assembled Gearbox. 2. INTRODUCTION ‹#› • Jetson Orin Nano (SVC) as the Central Control Unit. • Connected to Low Level Controller for low-level actuator control. • Actuators: TBW: DATAI via Arduino Mega and DAC BBW: Linear Actuator via DC Motor Driver SBW: Servo Motor via Servo Motor Driver • Feedback Mechanisms: Pressure sensor in BBW → STM32 Absolute angle sensor in SBW → STM32 • Power Sources: 48V battery → 24V & 12V via buck converters • Toggle Switches: Autonomous Switch ON/OFF Lateral Switch (SBW) Longitudinal Switch (TBW/BBW) System Architecture Diagram ‹#› Wiring Schematics Overview Power Lines 48V Battery Pack → Buck Converter ∘ 24V Output → MD10C Motor Driver & TiMOTION Actuator (BBW) ∘ 12V Output → Jetson Orin Nano (via regulator or step-down input) Communication & Logic Lines: Jetson Orin Nano ↔ STM32 (via UART) ∘ SBW - STM32 → DC Motor Driver: PWM (Speed) and DIR (Direction) pins ∘ BBW - STM32 → Servo Motor Driver via PWM TBW - Jetson → Arduino Mega → DAC → To Throttle Input ports of Traction motor controller ‹#› Wiring Schematics Overview Grounding: Common ground maintained between all logic and power components: ∘ STM32, Jetson, MD10C, Arduino, DAC4725, DATAI controller Safety & Isolation: Toggle switches isolate manual/autonomous modes for TBW, BBW, & SBW Dedicated fuses on each power rail to protect against overcurrent ‹#› Throttle-By-Wire System (TBW) • Manual: Throttle pedal → DATAI controller → 6-phase PMSM • Autonomous: Jetson → Arduino Mega → DAC4725 → Analog to DATAI • Toggle switch enables mode switching • Parallel wiring with common ground for Arduino, DAC, throttle pins ‹#› Brake-By-Wire System (SBW) • Jetson → STM32 → DC Motor Driver → Linear Actuator → Brake Pedal • Feedback: Pressure sensor → STM32 • Toggle switch selects autonomous/manual control. ‹#› Steer-By-Wire System (SBW) • Jetson → STM32 → Server Driver → Servo Motor → Rack & Pinion • Feedback via absolute angle sensor (AS5048A) • Autonomous Mode: Jetson ON, Servo Motor Active • Manual Mode: Jetson OFF, Steering via Wheel • Manual Override Possible via Mechanical Steering Link ‹#› Current Status & Future Integration While our Drive-by-Wire (DBW) system is still under active development.. Established a clear design framework and defined detailed signal flow for each subsystem Subsystem Outputs (Expected) ∘ TBW (Throttle-by-Wire)→ Smooth, controlled throttle operation ∘ BBW (Brake-by-Wire)→ Proportional braking response with safety feedback ∘ SBW (Steer-by-Wire)→ Real-time precision steering based on target angles THANK YOU

Submitter Information : Team Name TEAM E ZIBA RACERS Event Category E BAJA Team ID 262078 Contact Information Team Email sae.ziba r acers@ svecw.edu.in Name of Innovation Event Lead Harshitha Rudraraju Contact Number 9502459747 2 . Title of the I nvention : - Eco - Hybrid Composite Steering Wheel 3 . Idea Description This idea focuses on developing a steering wheel using a layered composite structure made from bamboo fiber, carbon fibre, and epoxy resin. The materials are arranged in multiple layers and moulded into a solid block or ring shape, which is then machined to obtain the final steering wheel geometry. Bamboo fiber acts as a natural and sustainable reinforcement, providing flexibility and vibration damping, while carbon fiber improves strength, stiffness, and durability. Epoxy resin binds the fibres together, offering impact resistance and a sm ooth surface finish. The proposed composite steering wheel functions similar to a conventional steering wheel by transmitting driver input through the steering column to control vehicle direction. However, compared to traditional metal or plastic steering wheels, this innovation is significantly lighter, has a higher strength - to - weight ratio, and reduces vibration transfer to the driver, thereby improving comfort and control. Additionally, the use of bamboo fiber makes the steering wheel more environmentall y friendly and cost - effective, while still meeting the functional and safety requirements 4. Technology Readiness Level TRL 3 Experimental Proof of Concept established . 5 . Novelty with Potential Applications The proposed steering wheel is a novel hybrid composite developed by combining bamboo fibre with carbon powder and epoxy resin, offering a sustainable and cost - effective alternative to conventional plastic and full carbon - fibre steering wheels. This hybrid material offers high strength - to - weight per formance at low cost, suitable for many practical uses. Beyond automotive steering wheels, it can be used in industrial control wheels, operator handles, and two - wheeler or ATV handlebars for lightweight, durable, and vibration - damped applications. 7 . Prior Art or Similar Solutions Existing steering wheel solutions include high - strength but costly carbon fiber, heavier and less sustainable plastic or polyurethane, and natural - fiber composites with limited strength. Our idea combines bamboo fiber with c arbon powder and epoxy resin, offering a sustainable, cost - effective alternative that maintains good structural strength, durability, and a smooth finish. 8 . This idea introduces an innovative approach to battery cooling system, integrating internal fluid coolant\ fins to revolutionize the heat dissipation process . Title of the Invention: - Adjustable Steering System Using Electroactive Polymer EAP\ Technology 3. Idea Description The adjustable steering system using electroactive polymer EAP\ technology represents a significant innovation in vehicle ergonomics and control. EAPs are materials that change shape when exposed to an electric field, allowing for precise movement without traditional mechanical components. This system leverages that capability to provide dynamic steering height adjustments, controlled via a microcontroller and a knob interface. By using a microcontroller, the system can regulate the electric input to the polymer, ensuring precise and smooth adjustments in real - time. The driver or user can simply turn a knob to select their desired steering height, making it a highly intuitive and responsive system. System Components and Operation 1. Electroactive Polymer Actuator : This provi ding the necessary force to adjust the steering height. The EAP will be connected to the steering column, allowing it to expand or contract based on user inputs. The system will be designed to handle the weight and forces typically experienced in steering operations, ensuring durability and reliability. 2. Microcontroller : It receives inputs from the user through the knob\ and controls the voltage supplied to the EAP actuator. Based on the desired steering height, the microcontroller will adjust the voltage, which in turn alters the shape of the EAP, raising or lowering the steering wheel. Advanced control algorithms can be implemented to ensure smooth transitions and prevent sudden movements. 3. Knob Interface : The user interface is a simple knob that can be rotated to increase or decrease the steering height. This user - friendly control system ensures that adjustments are intuitive and require minimal effort. The knob will have a feedback mechanism with digital display that informs the user of the current stee ring height. 4. Safety Systems : The system incorporates potentiometers to accurately measure the current position of the steering column. These sensors provide continuous feedback, ensuring that the column operates within safe limits. 4. Technology Readiness Level TRL 2 Technology concept or application formulated 5. Novelty with Potential Applications This adjustable steering system uniquely leverages Electroactive Polymer EAP\ technology to provide precise, quiet, and responsive height adjustments in steering columns. Unlike traditional mechanical or hydraulic systems, EAP actuators enable smooth transitions through electric field manipulation, reducing wear and boosting energy efficiency. The user can easily control adjustments via a knob interface connected to a microcontroller, enhancing both simplicity and durability. Applications Across Industries: Automotive: Offers customizable steering ad justments, improving driver comfort and ergonomics. Heavy Machinery: Benefits operators needing frequent adjustments for comfort and safety during extended shifts 7. Prior Art or Similar Solutions No, currently no one use Electroactive Polymer EAP\ technology to achieve steering column height adjustment. 8. files.extracted: CAE REPORT AMIGOS Vishnu Institute of Technology 1.ROLL CAGE: 1.1 Objective: The roll cage needs to provide structural support for the vehicle’s different sub-systems. Its primary function is to guarantee the safety of the driver in situations involving impact loads, rollovers and collisions. It should be stiff enough to compensate for the load transfer during cornering and other dynamic scenarios. 1.2 Material Properties: Material Selection of the roll cage plays crucial part in providing the desired strength, endurance, safety and reliability to the vehicle. To ensure the optimal selection of material, extensive research is carried out and comparison between the chemical and mechanical properties for various materials is done. After the extensive research in market there were three best options for us AISI 1018 AISI 4130 AISI 4140 Table no 1.2: Properties of materials Properties AISI 1018 AISI 4130 AISI 4140 Density (Kg/m3) 7870 7870 7870 Poisson’s ratio 0.29 0.29 0.29 Ultimate Tensile Strength (MPa) 440 640 655 Yield Strength (MPa) 365 560 415 Elasticity (GPa) 205 205 210 From the table no 1.2 we can see that the ultimate tensile strength for AISI 4140 is more than that of AISI 1018 and 4130.5AISI 4130 also consists of chromium, molybdenum and phosphorus which has various properties like high machinability and corrosion resistance. By comparing cost and availability of these material we came to conclusion that the availability of AISI 4130 is more and cost cutting than that of AISI 4140 conclusion that the cost of AISI 4130 is higher than that the AISI 1018 in all other required properties. Hence, we have selected AISI 4130 steel tubes for our roll cage manufacturing. 1.3 Front Impact: The front impact analysis was conducted under conditions simulating an impact at the front of the ATV. This assessment was performed to assess the stresses generated in the front portion, allowing for the observation of deformation and the factor of safety. The obtained results serve as a critical means to determine whether the roll cage can withstand such an impact. The crash analysis was carried out using Ansys 19.2 and serves as a crucial component in evaluating driver safety. Table no. 1.3.1: Element considerations Element Type Tetrahedral Element Size 1 mm Element order Linear 1.3.1 Boundary conditions: Time of Impact = 0.3 sec Velocity of the vehicle = 16.67 ms Rear suspension points are fixed Load applied on the front nose 1.3.2 Calculations: Deceleration suffered by vehicle, ut= 16.670.3 = 55.56 ms2 = 55.569.81 = 5.6G ~ 6G 1.3.3 Ansys Images: 1.4 Rear Impact: Rear impact analysis is conducted under conditions where the impact takes place at the rear section of the ATV. files.extracted: POWERTRAIN Abstract: A powertrain system is responsible for transmitting power from the engine to the wheels, enabling vehicle motion. It comprises the engine, transmission, and drivetrain, ensuring efficient power delivery, vehicle control, and mobility in diverse applications. Powertrain systems play a central role in defining a vehicle's performance, fuel efficiency, and functionality. Introduction: Power train is an interlink age of mechanism that transmits, power and torque from Engine to the Wheels of an automobile . Power train is also known as Transmission system. The objective of transmission to build a system capable of producing the torque required to drive the vehicle, as well as a gearbox capable of maintaining the required center distance betw een the input shaft connected to the secondary CVT and the output shaft connected to the half shaft. In addition, a wide range of gear ratios must be obtained, as well as maximum speed and high torque. The system must be affordable, lightweight, and effici ent. The vehicle with a gearbox is intended for an ATV All - Terrain Vehicle\ with the engine specifications shown below. Methodology: The project approach is based on Maximum Efficiency. The target was to get optimum design for every designed component. A s being a drivetrain, the target was to minimize rotating mass as much as we can thus leading to Optimum and Efficient design. files.extracted: 3 Suspension System: 3.1 Objective: The suspension system keeps a vehicle stable, safe, and comfortable by helping it navigate bumps and uneven roads. It consists of parts like tyres, springs, shock absorbers, hubs, and knuckles. These components work together to absorb shocks, lessen vibrations, and keep the wheels planted on the ground. This setup ensures the vehicle maintains good balance, improves handling, and provides proper control, even on rough surfaces. As a result, the driver enjoys a smooth and confident driving experience. 3.2 Introduction: CATIA V5 is used to create and refine several design concepts through a step-by-step improvement process that aims to reduce weight while maintaining the design strength and functionality. Each model is checked and improved using CATIA’s design, simulation, and optimisation tools. Finite Element Analysis (FEA) is performed to understand how the parts respond to different loads by studying stress, strain, and deformation, ensuring that the final model meets all structural and performance requirements. 3.3 Performance Target: Capable of achieving high cornering forces (1.2–1.5 g) while maintaining stable camber and sharp steering feedback. Ensures high-speed stability and quick, controlled response during rapid direction changes. Provides a neutral to slightly oversteering handling balance for predictable and confident vehicle behaviour. Offers strong cornering stability with reduced body roll and precise wheel control. Includes adjustable springs and dampers to fine-tune performance for street, track, or off-road conditions. Optimizes traction and grip, especially with a rear-biased weight distribution, for better acceleration and cornering performance. 3.4 Material Selection: Property Metric Tensile strength 670 Mpa Yield strength 460 Mpa Elongation 19.6% Modulus of elasticity 205Gpa Density 7.85 g/cm³ Percentage of carbon 0.28-0.33% Table no-1: Material Properties: AISI 4130 3.5 Suspension Selection: 3.5.1 Front Suspension: We selected a double wishbone suspension for the front because it offers a good balance of handling and comfort and is frequently found in performance cars. It makes the steering more responsive and enhances stability during cornering by enabling better control over wheel movement and alignment. 3.5.2 Rear Suspension: We chose an H-arm suspension setup for the back because it's conducive to providing stability at the rear, rather than allowing excessive articulation. This design aligns with our vehicle's stability needs and offers a solid, reliable structure for support. Given the fixed width of the track in the rear, we set the distance between the knuckle and frame mount at 18 inches. After considering in-depth analysis and simulation results, we identified 4130 steel tubing, 1.16 inch outside diameter, 1.65 mm wall thickness, as sufficiently strong and robust to use in the rear suspension design. files.extracted: POWERTRAIN OBJECTIVE: The aim of powertrain system is to transmit power efficiently from the engine to the wheels, enabling vehicle motion and ensuring optimal performance, fuel efficiency, and control. INTRODUCTION: The powertrain, also called the transmission system, transfers power and torque from the engine to the wheels. Its main goal is to provide the torque needed to drive the vehicle while maintaining the proper distance between the input shaft (from the CVT) and the output shaft (to the half shaft). The system should offer a wide range of gear ratios for both high torque and maximum speed, while being lightweight, efficient, and cost-effective. This setup is designed for an ATV using the engine specified below. Powertrain: The powertrain is the entire system that generates power and delivers it to the wheels. Includes: Engine Clutch (or torque converter) Transmission Driveshaft Differential Wheels Transmission: The transmission is a part of the powertrain that manages power from the engine and adjusts speed and torque. Includes: Gearbox (manual or automatic) Gear selector mechanism Sometimes includes CVT PERFORMANCE TARGET: The goal is to achieve smooth, responsive, and reliable power transmission, ensuring a comfortable ride with low noise and seamless operation. The system is designed to maximize fuel efficiency while maintaining high performance under varying loads and environmental conditions. METHODOLOGY: The project focused on achieving maximum efficiency by optimizing the design of each drivetrain component. The main objective was to minimize rotating mass, which directly contributes to improved performance and fuel efficiency. By reducing unnecessary weight and refining each part, the team aimed to develop a drivetrain that is both optimum in design and highly efficient in operation.
